Bringing The Elder Scrolls: Legends Back to Life

For those of you who are not already familiar, one of my absolute favorite games of all time was finally taken offline last year. I'm referring to The Elder Scrolls: Legends. It was a collectible card game and deckbuilder released by Bethesda.net that I downloaded on my smartphone way back in like 2017 or so. I grew to love the game dearly, and I played nearly up until they took their servers offline in 2025.

There are currently at least two separate projects to bring this game back to life for those who treasured it like I did. I'm not involved with either of them, but you can learn more about them here and here.

I have been trying out the re-creation over at tesl.online for the past week. I understand the project is very newly released, which I'm trying my best to keep in mind when I get frustrated after encountering some pretty maddening bugs. Although a couple were serious enough that I almost considered abandoning the site altogether, I tried to chill out and submitted the bug reports to the developer instead.

I'm sure it is a passion project and I don't want to seem like I don't appreciate their efforts. While I wouldn't recommend it just yet, I think it is very promising once they iron out a few of the more problematic issues I've encountered.

But this post isn't really supposed to be about these other projects. It's about something I decided to try to do on my own after spending some time with my old, favorite cards again in these new iterations.

I realized how much I simply missed the process of deckbuilding. It's almost like it acts as a de-stressing activity for me, at least.

I wondered if I could simply re-create a faithful simulation of the Arena deckbuilding process from the old game.

It would not actually allow you to play an Arena match. But it would let you choose the cards and build the deck you want from the choices given, like it worked in the original game.

For those not familiar with this, here is now it worked:

Most of the cards in The Elder Scrolls: Legends belong to one of five different card types/families: Strength (red), Endurance (purple), Willpower (yellow), Intelligence (blue), Agility (green), or Neutral.

The minimum number of cards for a deck that uses either all of the same color, or combines two of them, is 50 total. The maximum is 100. For decks using cards of three different colors, the minimum number of cards required is 75, and the max stays the same.

The most colors you can have in a single deck is three, plus neutral. You are allowed to have up to a total of three copies of the same card per deck.

Decks without any duplicate copies of the same card were known as Singleton decks.

Each combination of colors has its own family name in the game. They are as follows:
